<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Yann" />{{rh||I ÂRA''N''YAKA, 2 ADHYÂYA, 2 KHA''ND''A, 8.|169}}{{rule}}</noinclude><section begin="aranyaka1 adhyaya2" />is truth, and as endowed with the word {{lang|sa-Latl|satya}}, truth, the form of this day is perfect<ref>The commentator endeavours to make the meaning more natural by taking in the word {{lang|sa-Latl|prahantâ}}, he who kills the destroyer of truth. But considering the general character of these remarks, this is hardly necessary.</ref>.

2. That hymn is composed by Vasukra. Verily, Vasukra is Brahman, and that day is Brahman. Thus he obtains Brahman by means of Brahman<ref>Cf. I, 1, 3, 3.</ref>.

3. Here they say: 'Why then is that Marutvatîya hymn completed by the hymn of Vasukra?' Surely because no other ''Ri''shi but Vasukra brought out a Marutvatîya hymn, or divided it properly<ref>By separating the first t''rik''a from the second, and so forth.</ref>. Therefore that Marutvatîya hymn is completed by the hymn of Vasukra.

4. That hymn, {{lang|sa-Latl|asat su me}}, is not definitely addressed to any deity, and is therefore supposed to be addressed to Pra''g''âpati. Verily, Pra''g''âpati is indefinite, and therefore the hymn serves to win Pra''g''âpati.

5. Once in the hymn (Rv. X, 27, 22) he defines Indra ({{lang|sa-Latl|indrâya sunvat}}); therefore it does not fall off from its form, as connected with Indra.

6. He recites the hymn (Rv. VI, 17, 1) {{lang|sa-Latl|pibâ somam abhi yam ugra tarda''h''}}.

7. In the verse {{lang|sa-Latl|ûrvam gavyam mahi g''rin''âna indra}} the word {{lang|sa-Latl|mahi}}, great, occurs. Endowed with the word {{lang|sa-Latl|mahat}}, the form of this day is perfect.

8. That hymn is composed by Bharadvâ''g''a, and Bharadvâ''g''a. was he who knew most, who lived longest, and performed the greatest austerities among the ''Ri''shis, and by this hymn he drove away evil. Therefore if he recites the hymn of Bharadvâ''g''a,
